A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TRIM study, with readable main text and Appendices A–H. Pages 2–19 have identical extracted text and rendered images; the differences on page 1 are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing experiments in Section 5, alongside appendix results on latency, ablations, PRM robustness, model-pair generalization and GPQA-DIAMOND.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark comparisons, latency measurements and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The threshold, sequential-feature RL, aggregated-feature RL and POMDP routing policies are unchanged. Sections 3–4 and Appendix B retain identical actions, objectives and model formulations.

E1.justification: Coverage is unchanged, including GSM8k, MATH-500, AIME, OlympiadBench, Minerva Math, GPQA-DIAMOND and ProcessBench-based supervision. The additional domains and noise scenarios in the appendices already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same BERT, MF, SW Ranking, Smoothie, AutoMix and AutoMix-PRM comparisons. The oracle comparison in Figure 2 and One-Step Thr comparator in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented splits, model pairs, metrics, budgets and testing procedures are identical. This includes the MATH training/MATH-500 evaluation setup, approximately 50–50 AIME split, and appendix latency and robustness protocols.

E4.justification: The latency analysis, intervention-count analysis, full-takeover ablation, PRM-noise experiment, model-pair generalization tests and PRM effectiveness assessment are retained without changes in Appendices A and D–H.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing oracle-frontier shading and PRM distribution analyses remain identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports TRIM-Agg's MATH-500 CPT(95%) as 79.58 tokens (17.21%) in both versions, and Appendix H retains the AIME AUC-ROC of 0.8397.

T1.justification: The sequential routing formulation, RL objective, metric definitions and Appendix B POMDP formalization are identical, including the latent-state definitions and irrecoverability assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about targeted stepwise intervention, cost efficiency and cross-dataset generalization. The abstract's punctuation edit does not alter claim meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of budget-dependent performance, transferable routing behavior and PRM noise remain unchanged. The qualifications concerning model compatibility and unimplemented system optimizations in API-based experiments are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit Project Page and Code hyperlinks on page 1, providing resource-access information absent from v1. Implementation details and hyperparameters in Appendix G and Table 12 are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked resources' contents or completeness.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and comparisons with prior routing, process-supervision and speculative-decoding research are identical. The new project and code links do not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: Page 1 adds resource labels, updates version and preprint dates, and replaces the en dash in 'accuracy–cost' with a hyphen. The scientific prose, section ordering and appendix structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: A centered resource-link row with icons is added below the authors, slightly shifting the first-page text. All seven figures, twelve tables, captions and layouts on pages 2–19 are identical.

improvement.justification: The new project and code links give readers resource locations absent from v1, modestly improving access and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. This benefit is limited to the supplied pointers; the PDFs cannot verify the linked code's availability or completeness.
